statement: What fraction of the 23,138-row qualification plan can EVER be covered from this environment, and what needs a different one. Computed as leaves x runnable profiles, which is an UPPER BOUND: it does not model the plan's 43 predeclared exclusion rows nor per-profile applicability, so the plan's own row count is 23,132 + 6 driver rows while this arithmetic yields 23,700. Treat the percentages as approximate ceilings, not as a second denominator.

blocked_profiles.U0: pristine (unstaged) checkout: needs a SECOND full build tree alongside the existing 16 GB one. Disk-blocked here, measured. Unblocked by a bigger runner, not by any code change.
blocked_profiles.U3: storage factory refuses at runtime: ProfileUnavailable { profile: "U3" }. The product profile is not implemented; this is a product gap, not an environment limit.
blocked_profiles.U4: storage factory refuses at runtime: ProfileUnavailable { profile: "U4" }. Same: a product gap.

CUCUMBER.note: all 47 catalogued feature files and all 4,099 scenarios are reachable via cargo, and per-scenario outcomes already exist in the sealed U1/U2 bundles. The blocker is the Scenario Outline name join, not execution.

FAILPOINT.note: not observable per leaf: 22 fail points are iterated INSIDE a single #[test] and libtest prints one line for the case. Covering these needs an upstream change that emits one case per fail point, not a harness change here. Deriving 44 passes from one passing loop is inference, not evidence.

SCRIPT.note: //tool/test:simulate-crash has no referent in the pinned upstream tree (confirmed against Bazel's own graph). This is a catalogue defect, kept rather than deleted: silently removing a plan row is how a denominator shrinks.

STATIC_CHECK.note: 63 of the 141 are rustfmt_test and ARE faithfully runnable with the same tool; the other 78 are checkstyle/checkstyle_license, which run TypeDB's Java Checkstyle with an MPL header config fetched by Bazel. A Python reimplementation of the header property would be a SUBSTITUTE, not the upstream tool, so those rows are not claimed on one.
